pergunta: Does the retention law (eq:R, mean field) predict the REAL nodal retention (val and test) at more than two geometry points (g,b)? Today there is a comparison only at (g,b)=(10,2) and (5,2); this test adds b=1 and b=3 km with g=10km, in the 16 g10 cells, 20 split_seeds.

criterio.alegacao: A1 (Geometry: the retention of an eroded block follows a closed-form law with finite-domain corrections)
criterio.pergunta: Does the retention law (eq:R, mean field) predict the REAL nodal retention (val and test) at more than two geometry points (g,b)? Today there is a comparison only at (g,b)=(10,2) and (5,2); this test adds b=1 and b=3 km with g=10km, in the 16 g10 cells, 20 split_seeds.
criterio.hipotese: The relative error (lei_campo_medio(q_realizado) - retencao_nodal_real)/retencao_nodal_real, on the TEST set, varies monotonically with b (smaller b -> smaller error in absolute value), without changing sign between b=1,2,3, and the order of magnitude of the error at b=2 (already published, -6.2% to -6.9%) is preserved at the neighbouring points (b=1 and b=3).
limiar_de_aceitacao: sign of the mean relative test error (over the 20 seeds, per cell) is the SAME at the three points b=1,2,3 (g=10) -- no sign change
|erro_relativo_teste(b=1)| <= |erro_relativo_teste(b=2)| <= |erro_relativo_teste(b=3)| (monotonicity in b, violation tolerance: at most 2/16 cells out of order, due to sampling noise)

erro_relativo_teste(b=2) recomputed here lies within [-6.9%, -6.2%] (order of magnitude of the already published number); b=1 and b=3 stay in the same order of magnitude (factor <=3x in absolute value)
criterio.o_que_refuta: sign change of the relative error between b=1, b=2 and b=3 on the test set; OR gross non-monotonicity (more than 2/16 cells out of the expected order); OR relative error at b=2 outside one decade of the published range (-6.2% to -6.9%) -- any of these overturns 'the law holds at more than two points' and A1 is left without support from this test (it goes to a note, not to the article)
criterio.metodo_declarado: for (g,b) in {(10,1),(10,2),(10,3)} in the 16 g10 cells and (5,2) in the 4 bauru g5 cells, 20 split_seeds (SEEDS_20 from varredura_fracao_valida_r3.py), reconstruct the actual partition via split_e_metricas_edt (varredura_split_geometria.py, EDT method already validated <1e-3 against exact cKDTree in the module itself), fractions 70/15/remainder-test (FRACS); compute q_te=k_te/N, q_va=1-k_tr/N (k,N in actual pixels of the cell); compare the actual NODAL retention (n_apos_buffer/n_antes_buffer) with eq:R evaluated at the realised q (closed formula copied, without editing, from analysis/fismat_sympy_eqR.py lines 42 and 118-149 -- eqR_num and lattice_retention/raster_counts for the finite-domain correction, reimplemented locally by literal copy so as not to execute the other script with write side effects outside pasta_saida)
criterio.fixado_por: fixed in internal/note_16.md, 25/09/2026, BEFORE running the script v3_1.4_varredura_b_lei_vs_nodal.py
criterio.nao_amplia_a_varredura: roadmap rule D5 -- only the 4 listed (g,b) points; no additional grid

errata.bug_identificado: The function R_law(g,b,q) (eq:R, closed form) was CORRECT, but the q FED into it was WRONG: q_te_realizado = n_te_apos_buffer(pixels) / N_total(pixels=3600x3600) and q_va_realizado = 1 - n_tr(pixels)/N_total(pixels) had been used -- a fraction of PIXELS after buffer erosion, which varies by seed. The correct q (used by R3-c, fismat_sympy_eqR.json and verificador_eqR_resultado.json) is the fraction of BLOCKS (not pixels): q_te = n_blocos_test/n_blocos_total, q_va = 1 - n_blocos_train/n_blocos_total, with the NOMINAL block counts (FRACS 0.70/0.15/0.15 rounded over n_blocos_total = number of g x g blocks that fit in the cell domain) -- these counts are DETERMINISTIC per (cell,g), independent of split_seed (only which block goes to which partition changes, not how many). For bauru Q1 g10b2: n_blocos_total=132, n_blocos_test_nominal=20 -> q_te=20/132=0.151515, R_law(10,2,0.151515)=0.433953 -- matches to 6 decimal places the number already published/reproduced (0.43395). The function split_e_metricas_edt() already returned these counts in the field n_blocos (never used in v1 of this script). CORRECTED: q now comes from n_blocos/n_blocos_total (via assign_groups, without recomputing the sweep -- n_blocos depend only on (cell,g), reused from the imported module itself).
errata.segundo_ajuste_necessario: The original aggregation also averaged, per cell, the MEAN ACROSS SEEDS of (lei-nodal_s)/nodal_s (mean-of-ratios). Since the law is CONSTANT across seeds (it depends only on cell/g/b) and the nodal retention VARIES per seed, mean-of-ratios != (lei-media(nodal))/media(nodal) (ratio-of-means) by Jensen's inequality (1/x is convex). The number already published in the draft uses RATIO-OF-MEANS (confirmed against R3-c: bauru g10b2 te = -6.8587% == (0.433953-0.465908)/0.465908). Ratio-of-means is now reported as the PRIMARY definition (field *_RATIO_OF_MEANS in resumo_por_gb) and mean-of-ratios as a secondary field (erro_relativo_test_media_entre_celulas_MEAN_OF_RATIOS_por_seed), both explicitly named.
errata.achado_removido: The finding "achado_ambiguidade_definicao" of the previous round (which said that the published number only matched as an absolute difference in pp, not as a relative error) was CAUSED BY THE q BUG and is FALSE -- removed from this artifact. With the correct q (fraction of blocks), the RELATIVE error matches the published number directly (RATIO-OF-MEANS), without needing reinterpretation as pp.
errata.nao_verificado_novo: none -- the reconciliation against the 3 independent artifacts (R3-c, fismat_sympy_eqR.json, verificador_eqR_resultado.json) closed with agreement to >=6 decimal places for bauru g10b2 and g5b2
